title: Quickstart: send your first meter event
summary: Create a meter, send one event with the HTTP API, and see it on a draft invoice in under ten minutes.
body:
This quickstart uses a sandbox account and the HTTP API. The SDKs wrap the same calls.

1. Create a meter

In the dashboard, open Meters → New meter. Name it api.calls, aggregation count(), unit call.

2. Send an event

POST /v1/events
{ "meter": "api.calls", "customer": "cus_test_01",
  "quantity": 1, "idempotency_key": "first-event-1" }

3. See it rated

Open Customers → cus_test_01 → Draft invoice. The line shows one call, and its explain tree shows one event received, zero duplicates.

Next

Read Idempotency keys and late events before you send production traffic.

title: Meters, dimensions and aggregation
summary: How raw events become billable quantities: meters, the five aggregation functions, and when to use a dimension instead of a new meter.
body:
A meter names a thing you measure and how to roll it up. A dimension is a key on the event you may split or price by.

Rule of thumb

Create a new meter when the unit changes (calls vs minutes). Use a dimension when the unit is the same but the price or reporting differs (region, model).

FunctionUse for
count()API calls, requests
sum(quantity)Minutes, rows, bytes
max(quantity)Peak concurrency
unique(field)Active devices, distinct keys

title: Idempotency keys and late events
summary: Why every event needs an idempotency key, how long keys are kept, and what happens to events that arrive after the late window.
body:
Send a stable key per logical event — a request ID works. Abacene keeps keys for 35 days and drops repeats before aggregation.

Late events

Within the window, a late event re-rates the open period. After the window, it posts to the next invoice as a dated adjustment. Closed invoices are never rewritten.

title: Pricing models: tiers, volume, packages and credits
summary: Worked examples of the five pricing models and prepaid credits, with the invoice line each one produces.
body:
Graduated tiers price each unit at the rate of its tier; volume tiers price every unit at the rate of the tier the total lands in. Packages bill per block. Minimums and caps wrap any model.

Credits are applied after rating, oldest grant first, and appear as their own line.

title: Using the invoice explain API
summary: Fetch explain trees for invoice lines, page through dimension splits, and build your own in-app billing page on top.
body:
Customer guide. Authenticate with a restricted key that has invoices:read.

GET /v1/invoices/{id}/lines/{n}/explain?expand=dimensions

Responses are cacheable for closed invoices: a closed invoice's explain tree never changes. For open invoices, cache for no more than five minutes.

Building a customer billing page

Most customers render the top three levels (price, aggregate, dimensions) and link to a CSV export for the rest.

title: Month-end reconciliation runbook
summary: The checklist finance teams use on the first business day: close the period, review adjustments, export journal entries, match payments.
body:
Customer runbook.

  1. Confirm the late-event window has closed for every meter (Dashboard → Periods).
  2. Review the adjustments list: anything over $500 gets a second look.
  3. Export journal entries (CSV or SFTP) and import to your accounting system.
  4. Run the reconciliation report; totals should tie to the journal export to the cent.
  5. Match payments from your processor export; work the unmatched list.

Typical time: 40 minutes for 300 customers (story).

title: Rate card versioning and price changes
summary: How to change a price safely: new version, effective date, customer notice, and how in-flight periods are rated.
body: Customer guide. Never edit a live rate card; create a version with an effective date at a period boundary. Periods that started before the date are rated on the old version.

title: SSO with SAML or OpenID Connect
summary: Connect your identity provider, map groups to Abacene roles, and require SSO for every dashboard user.
body:
Customer guide for Scale and Enterprise. Abacene supports SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect. Map IdP groups to the roles finance, support, engineering and admin.

Once SSO is required, password sign-in is disabled for everyone except one break-glass admin.

title: Contract-aware rating (beta guide)
summary: How to model ramps, amendments and minimum commitments in the contract-aware rating beta, and how to compare results against your current rate cards.
body:
Beta guide. Run contract-aware rating in shadow mode first: it rates every period both ways and shows differences without changing invoices.

Shadow mode checklist

  • Pick five customers with ramps or amendments
  • Run two full periods in shadow
  • Every difference should be explained by a contract term

title: Usage forecasting (beta guide)
summary: Turn on forecasts for a subset of customers, read the confidence band, and send feedback on accuracy.
body: Beta guide. Enable forecasting per customer from Customers → Forecasting. Compare projections with actuals at period close; the beta report shows mean absolute error per meter.
